# Discovery for the no-token invocation

No PR token was given, so argument-resolution discovery runs first. It runs before the set-vs-single branch, the continuation record, the run folder, tracker init and provisioning.

**What has not happened yet in any of the four runs:**
- No run folder or continuation record exists.
- No `plan_tracker` stages are initialized.
- No worktree is provisioned.
- No SHA is assessed. Neither verification nor the brief has assessed a head.

## Main run

### Commands already run (results in hand)

1. `git remote get-url origin` returned `acme/widgets`.
2. `gh api user --jq .login` returned `alex`.
3. `gh api user/teams --paginate ...` returned an empty list. That is readable, not `unreadable`.
4. The two separate `gh pr list -R acme/widgets ... --state open --limit 1000` calls both exited 0:
   - one with `--author @me`
   - one with `--search 'review-requested:@me'`

   Both results are well-formed arrays below the limit. The union by number holds #19, #22, #27, #31, #38 and #40.

### Filter

- #31 is excluded because it is a draft.
- #38 is excluded because its review decision is exactly `APPROVED`.
- That leaves #19, #22 and #27 with `CHANGES_REQUESTED`, and #40 with `REVIEW_REQUIRED`.

### Review lookups, one shell call each, in ascending PR number

5. Lookup for #19 (`gh api graphql ...` piped to `jq`): exit 0, stdout `answered`. **Kept.**
6. Lookup for #22: exit 0, stdout `unanswered`. **Excluded** from both the list and the gated set.
7. Lookup for #27: exit 0, stdout `answered`. **Kept.**

#40 is kept without a lookup.

### Sort

Survivors are sorted by additions plus deletions, then by number: #40 (3), #27 (5), #19 (9).

### What the user reads

This is its own intermediate message. It has no marker and asks nothing.

**Open PRs to gate, smallest first:**
- [#40](https://github.com/acme/widgets/pull/40) +3 -0, by jo, requested from you, no ticket - sorts widgets
- [#27](https://github.com/acme/widgets/pull/27) +5 -0, by jo, requested from you, no ticket - restores widget colors
- [#19](https://github.com/acme/widgets/pull/19) +9 -0, by jo, requested from you, no ticket - shows widget names

### Outcome

There are two or more matches on pi, so discovery re-enters set routing with `source: discovered`. It passes these sorted origin URL tokens:

1. `https://github.com/acme/widgets/pull/40`
2. `https://github.com/acme/widgets/pull/27`
3. `https://github.com/acme/widgets/pull/19`

The run stops here, before set admission, gathering or provisioning.

## Isolated run: failed call

Steps 1 to 4 and the filter are identical to the main run. The first lookup, for #19, exits 1 with empty stdout. Discovery stops at once:
- The #22 and #27 lookups never run.
- No list is printed.
- Nothing is routed.

gauntlet: stuck discovery failed: HTTP 502: Bad Gateway

discovery failed: HTTP 502: Bad Gateway

## Isolated run: unreadable lookup

Steps 1 to 4 and the filter are identical to the main run. The #19 lookup exits 1 with stdout `malformed`. Discovery stops before the remaining lookups, the list and routing.

gauntlet: stuck discovery failed: malformed review lookup for #19

discovery failed: malformed review lookup for #19

## Isolated run: incomplete lookup

Steps 1 to 4 and the filter are identical to the main run. The #19 lookup exits 1 with stdout `incomplete`. Discovery stops before the remaining lookups, the list and routing.

gauntlet: stuck discovery failed: incomplete review lookup for #19

discovery failed: incomplete review lookup for #19

1. #19 returns `answered`; retain it.
2. #22 returns `unanswered`; exclude it. The later plain comment does not change this result.
3. #27 returns `answered`; retain it.

Retain #40 without a lookup. Sort the remaining PRs by additions plus deletions, then number.

The user reads:

**Open PRs to gate, smallest first:**
- [#40](https://github.com/acme/widgets/pull/40) +3 -0, by jo, requested from you, no ticket - sort widgets
- [#27](https://github.com/acme/widgets/pull/27) +5 -0, by jo, requested from you, no ticket - restore widget colors
- [#19](https://github.com/acme/widgets/pull/19) +9 -0, by jo, requested from you, no ticket - show widget names

Send **40, 27, 19**, in that order, to set routing using their origin URLs and `source: discovered`. Stop this narration before admission.

### Isolated run: failed call

Run the review lookup for #19 first. It fails; use only the first stderr line. Run no lookup for #22 or #27, print no PR list, and send nothing to set routing.

The user reads:

gauntlet: stuck discovery failed
discovery failed: HTTP 502: Bad Gateway

Run the review lookup for #19 first. Its supplied result is `malformed` with exit status 1. Run no lookup for #22 or #27, print no PR list, and send nothing to set routing.

gauntlet: stuck discovery failed
discovery failed: malformed review lookup for #19

### Isolated run: incomplete lookup

anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: All five facts moved from fails to holds as intended, and Before held none, so nothing was lost. Before excluded every CHANGES_REQUESTED PR on the projected decision alone, ran no lookups, listed only #40 on the single-PR path, and produced the same result in all three failure runs. After runs the lookup for #19, #22 and #27 only, in ascending order, keeps the two `answered` PRs, drops the `unanswered` #22, lists #40, #27, #19 under the plural heading and routes those three in that order. In each failure run it stops at the #19 lookup with the exact `discovery failed: ...` text (first stderr line only for the 502), printing no list and routing nothing. To keep this stable, keep the wording that states lookups run only for surviving CHANGES_REQUESTED PRs in ascending number, that any non-zero exit stops before the list, and that the failure message uses the first error line or the named malformed/incomplete form with the PR number. One thing to watch: After prints an extra `gauntlet: stuck discovery failed: ...` line before each stop line; if the stop message is meant to be the sole output, tighten the wording to say which single line is emitted, since a stricter fact could read the duplicate as a deviation.
